reviewer_summary.question: Why must a chosen word be processed before choosing the following word, and what earlier work can each layer reuse?
reviewer_summary.takeaway: Choosing blue uses the previous word’s finished result; blue must then make its own result, while saved keys and values let it reuse earlier reading preparation.

findings.problem: The first multiplication and the separate input-dependency distinction arrive in the same beat.

resolution.note: Put the input-dependency explanation in a new beat after the multiplication, in the same persistent diagram.

findings.problem: Reader independence is stated before a second reader uses the source preparation.

resolution.note: Name the concrete key only. Demonstrate unchanged source preparation when is later reads The before drawing any independence conclusion.

findings.problem: The replay begins before its unanswered question is spoken.

resolution.note: Ask what work would have to be repeated without the saved entries before rewinding and comparing the two starting states.

findings.problem: A hypothetical zero interrupts the incomplete actual reading and creates competing numbers.

resolution.note: Remove the hypothetical. Teach the zero-plus-one consequence on the actual negative-match case during blue’s reading.

findings.problem: The total picture previews division while narration is adding.

resolution.note: The total guide/note now describe addition only; division appears with the actual division beat.

findings.problem: The proof picture announces blue reading valid preparation before that reading is shown.

resolution.note: Keep the proof picture to unchanged earlier inputs/entries only; demonstrate blue’s reading in its later actual pass.

findings.problem: Pass naming after the complete mechanism feels like a new lesson.

resolution.note: Attach prefill to the just-completed supplied-text pass and decode to the just-completed blue pass, separated by their actual work. Remove the late vocabulary transition.
